clue.text: Has the ability to write poetry

parts.note: someone who has the ability to do something can do it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that someone is gifted enough to compose verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'write' only links the wordplay to the definition here; the surface reads it as a verb about composing.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is one of the main divisions of a long poem, so it is a piece of verse.

clue.text: Love is in short measure in this area

indicators.note: the letter for love is placed inside the word for short

parts.note: curt means short or brusque
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
a yard is a measure of length

explanation.surface: A remark that love sits within a short measure in some region.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtyard is an enclosed open space beside a building, an area of ground.

clue.text: Impressive gold coin

explanation.surface: An impressive gold coin, perhaps in a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble means grand and imposing; the noble was also an old English gold coin.

clue.text: Remain too long having finished visit

parts.note: something finished is over
a stay is a visit somewhere

explanation.surface: A guest lingering after a visit has really ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay one's welcome is to linger past the proper time.

clue.text: Bait's now a problem for a seagoing man

indicators.note: letters that are a problem are troubled, so they are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler finds bait hard to come by for a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator is 'problem'; the fodder BAITSNOW plus A rearranges to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosun is a ship's officer in charge of equipment and crew, a sailor.

clue.text: A European cricketer about fifty

indicators.note: the word for a cricketer goes around the Roman numeral, as about means surrounding

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A European cricket player who has made around fifty runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balt is a native of one of the Baltic states, such as Latvia or Estonia.

clue.text: Bet at cards — come a cropper, being inattentive

indicators.note: to come a cropper is to fall badly, so the letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A card player places a bet and loses badly through not paying attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abstracted is lost in thought and not noticing what goes on around them.

clue.text: Way to go on setting the pace

explanation.surface: Advice on how to walk while leading a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a manner of walking forward, and one's stride is the length of step that sets a pace.

clue.text: Risk coming over the river

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the second

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A dangerous trip arriving across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A risky undertaking or exciting enterprise; to venture something is to hazard it.

clue.text: Never vacillating shows courage

indicators.note: vacillating means wavering back and forth, so the letters shift around

explanation.surface: Steady resolve never wavering demonstrates bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is boldness or daring, as in having the nerve to act.

clue.text: They may well get held up in bad weather

definitions.text: They may well get held up in bad weather

parts.words: They may well get held up in bad weather
parts.note: held up seems to mean delayed, like trains in a storm, but means raised overhead for rain shelter

explanation.surface: Things likely to be delayed by storms.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain shields carried open above the head are raised when it pours.

clue.text: A vagrant involved in some controversy

indicators.note: the letters are involved within part of the following word, so they lie inside it

explanation.surface: A tramp caught up in a public row.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is a wanderer with no settled home.

clue.text: The first true believer

parts.note: taken as written
first is abbreviated as 1st, with the figure read as the letter I

explanation.surface: The original faithful follower.
explanation.walkthrough: First is written 1ST, and the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist believes in God, a person of religious faith.

clue.text: Caution a woman

explanation.surface: A warning about a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is careful good sense; it is also a girl's name.

clue.text: It burrows in the sand to cut down attack

parts.note: a razor is the tool used to cut down stubble
to shell is to attack with artillery

explanation.surface: Some creature digs into a beach in order to mount an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The razor clam is a long narrow mollusc that digs down into beaches.

clue.text: Look for a soft fruit cane needing attention

parts.note: taken as written
p, short for piano, is the musical sign for soft
a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: the word needs attention, so it is put right by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Searching for a fruit cane that needs care in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: One's look is the way one seems to others, one's outward aspect.

clue.text: Wrapping up well, the body not getting any younger!

parts.note: a pack is a body or group, as of wolves or hounds
someone not getting any younger is ageing, here spelt without the E

explanation.surface: An elderly person told to dress warmly as they get older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' just links the parts. AGING is the shorter spelling of ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: Packaging is the material that encloses goods, so it is a covering.

clue.text: A pound of tobacco?

explanation.surface: Asking about a pound weight of smoking leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Quid is British slang for one pound sterling; a quid is also a plug of chewing leaf.

clue.text: Wanted to introduce pop, but lost all hope

indicators.note: to introduce is to bring in, so the word for pop is placed inside

parts.note: wanted means desired
pop and pa are both words for father

explanation.surface: Someone wanted to bring in fizzy drinks but gave up.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to give up all expectation of things improving.

clue.text: Cover up a Conservative's procrastinating

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political cover-up by a delaying Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory means slow and given to delay, putting things off.

clue.text: Note one gets little fish

parts.note: D is a musical note
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A message reports that someone caught a small fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The dace is a small freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: "I have a left shoulder-blade that is a miracle of ", claimed Katisha

definitions.text: "I have a left shoulder-blade that is a miracle of ", claimed Katisha

parts.words: "I have a left shoulder-blade that is a miracle of ", claimed Katisha
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank line sung by Katisha, the elderly lady in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Mikado

explanation.surface: A quotation from a vain operatic character boasting of her shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: Katisha, in The Mikado, boasts that her left shoulder-blade is a miracle of this quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the noun for great beauty, completing the quoted lyric.

clue.text: Make much of top men joining firm

parts.note: COs are commanding officers, the top men of a unit
set means firm or solid

explanation.surface: Executives arriving at a company get pampered.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper or fuss over someone.

clue.text: In the main this isn't mounted

definitions.text: In the main this isn't mounted

parts.words: In the main this isn't mounted
parts.note: the main is the sea, and a creature named after a steed living there is never ridden

explanation.surface: Something that, generally speaking, is not ridden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly' but means in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A small upright marine fish with a head shaped like a pony's.

clue.text: Daphne given the brush off?

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Daphne is rebuffed by a suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given the brush off' looks like rejection; Daphne is a genus of woody flowering plants, and 'off' scrambles BRUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne is a genus of small woody garden plants, so one is an example of the bush type.

clue.text: Had recurring trouble getting back, having made a bloomer

indicators.note: recurring here means running back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: getting back means returning, so this word too is read in reverse

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: After repeated problems in returning, someone makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurring' turns HAD into DAH, and 'getting back' turns AIL into LIA. A bloomer is also slang for a blunder, the false path.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is anything that flowers, and this garden plant has showy blooms.

clue.text: Scientist's local branch

explanation.surface: A researcher's nearby office.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Oliver Lodge was a British physicist who worked on radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Lodge was a noted physicist; a lodge is also a local chapter of a society such as the Freemasons.

clue.text: A blockhead the French find clever

parts.note: taken as written
the head, or first letter, of the word block
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people think a dimwit is clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blockhead' is read as the head of 'block', not a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilled and competent.

clue.text: Bars for fliers

explanation.surface: Pubs for pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: Rails are horizontal bars; rails are also marsh birds, such as the water rail.

clue.text: Get the needle and add fictitious details

explanation.surface: Someone becomes annoyed and starts making things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider is to decorate cloth with needlework, and also to embellish a story.

clue.text: The musicians' game?

parts.note: the word names a table game played with balls and pins, and also a short light piece of music

explanation.surface: Asking what pastime players of instruments enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a short light piano piece and also a board game like billiards.

clue.text: Admit defeat and return

explanation.surface: Give up and go home.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to surrender; a yield is also the return on an investment.
